name: RIPPLE
oneLiner: Civic reporting PWA that classifies the photo on the phone, before it uploads

metrics.label: on-device inference, p50, against a 3,000 ms budget
database assertions on real PostgreSQL 17, 0 failures
unit tests, from zero five months earlier
Lighthouse Performance on the mobile preset — below its own gate

headline.claim: Four of this project's own green checks could never have failed: a typecheck gate that checked zero files, a PWA regex that accepted either answer, RLS tests handed the credential they were meant to prove unobtainable, and a column REVOKE that silently cannot subtract from a table GRANT.

honest: The front end is deployed and the PWA, map, offline shell and on-device classifier all work at the live URL — but there is no backend behind it. The Supabase project it was built against no longer resolves and has deliberately not been re-provisioned, so nothing that reads or writes data functions: reports do not load or submit, and Storage, Auth, Edge Function deployment and Realtime delivery are all unproven. The database layer itself is verified by execution against a local PostgreSQL 17 (27 migrations, 102 assertions, 0 failures); what is unverified is specifically what Supabase-the-service adds on top. The classifier pipeline is complete and benchmarked but runs on a generic ImageNet backbone, so no accuracy claim is made — and first load is ~7MB against a stated <5s-on-4G budget, which is why mobile Lighthouse Performance is 68 and fails the project's own gate.

built.audit: Twenty sprints were marked complete on the criterion 'TypeScript and ESLint pass with zero errors'; an audit measuring the repo against its own checkmarks found seven false subtask claims, zero test files against a 'no test, no merge' rule, and a Supabase backend that had been deleted.
repaired: GPS failure was an unrecoverable dead end — the hook cleared its loading flag with latitude still null, leaving Submit permanently disabled with no error and no way forward
All eight Edge Function validation messages were unreachable; users saw 'Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code' instead of the real reason
Two RLS policies named _own were written USING (true) — any anonymous caller could delete any upvote, and every notification email was world-readable
reporter_token was world-readable even after that fix, because RLS is row-level and filters no columns; the harvest-then-replay chain succeeded end to end until column-level privileges landed
pnpm build was failing at HEAD on a type error, hidden because the gate ran `vite build` (skipping tsc -b) and `tsc --noEmit` against a root tsconfig with files: []
The service worker served the offline page to online users: navigateFallback pointed at offline.html and a workbox NavigationRoute matches every navigation, breaking every deep link
Three colour tokens were below the WCAG AA contrast floor in an app for reporting accessibility hazards — and the first fix changed nothing visible, because the palette is defined in three places
The offline queue only flushed while the user was on /report; rate limiting was localStorage theatre defeated by one devtools click
measured: Inference p50 15ms / p95 22ms with real LiteRT WASM against a real int8 .tflite in a real browser — against a 3,000ms budget
27 migrations and 102 assertions against a throwaway PostgreSQL 17.11, including attacks run as the anon role
Realtime read from a pgoutput replication slot directly: 13 frames, 1 INSERT, 2 UPDATE, 1 DELETE
Model resolves from Cache Storage byte-identical (5,434,517 bytes) with the network cut, and all five routes render from cache
Lighthouse on both presets — desktop 96, mobile 68 — which showed the 92 previously on record was a desktop number quoted without its form factor

decisions.why: TF.js is frozen at 4.22.0 (Oct 2024). Reading @litertjs/core's own .d.ts showed CompiledModel.run(Tensor[]) and Tensor.fromTypedArray() are native, so preprocessing with Canvas removes TF.js outright rather than swapping it — Google's own quickstart would have reintroduced it purely for tensor plumbing.

decisions.what: Postgres full-text search instead of Elasticsearch
decisions.why: A generated tsvector column cannot drift from its source, so the sync Edge Function, the nightly re-index and the proxy all cease to exist rather than being maintained — for a product with zero users and a $16/month bill. Deferred, not rejected; useSearch is backend-agnostic.
The photo never leaves the phone to be understood — only as evidence, and only after Submit. A privacy architecture first and a latency win second.

decisions.what: Category identity moved from colour to monospace glyph
decisions.why: The design system permits one accent, so colour cannot encode ten categories — and it never did: two categories already shared a hex. Shape survives greyscale, colour blindness and low outdoor contrast.

decisions.what: Community consensus flags 'fixed', it does not set it
decisions.why: Three confirmation photos set community_suggests_fixed and stop there. Consensus is evidence, not authority; the status belongs to the council.

ownerGated: OG1 — re-provision Supabase, apply 27 migrations, deploy 6 Edge Functions, create the storage buckets
OG2 — training data for the fine-tuned civic classifier (~500 images/category across 10 categories)
OG10 — legal content for the Terms page: 12 placeholders (entity, ABN, governing law, liability). Nothing was invented.
OG4 — Elasticsearch (recommend continued deferral; it costs money and Postgres FTS covers the use case)
OG5 — Resend API key for status-change email
OG6 — real-device testing: iOS Safari install, OS camera confirmation, mid-range Android latency
OG7 — ABS council boundary polygons to replace the overlapping placeholders
